mainTopic: Pausing within phrases (ברוך הבא, יהא שמיה רבא), customs and the ברכה for הלל with the rule of עובר לעשייתן, and buying a לולב and אתרוג during שביעית without giving holy money to an עם הארץ.
overview: This amud finishes the discussion about pausing in the middle of a phrase. רבא says not to split 'יהא שמיה רבא' from 'מברך' in קדיש, and רב ספרא rejects him: the completing word makes the meaning clear either way. The גמרא then explains two lines of the משנה about הלל. For repeating verses, a ברייתא says רבי repeated verses and רבי אלעזר בן פרטא added more, which אביי explains as repeating from 'אודך' onward. For the ברכה, אביי says custom decides only the ברכה after הלל. The ברכה before it is a real מצוה, based on שמואל's rule that every מצוה is blessed 'עובר לעשייתן', and three פסוקים prove that 'עובר' means 'before'. A new משנה then teaches that during שביעית a buyer pays for the לולב and gets the אתרוג as a gift. The גמרא explains that if the seller refuses, the אתרוג's price is hidden in the לולב's price. The reason is that holy שביעית money may not be handed to an עם הארץ beyond three meals' worth. The ברייתא's fix for money already handed over continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב ספרא rejects the earlier rule about pausing in ברוך הבא
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא rejects רבא's earlier rule that one should not pause between 'ברוך הבא' and 'בשם ה''. Either way, the second half clearly finishes the thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רב ספרא said to רבא:] 'משה, did you speak well?! Rather, both there and here, it is just completing the matter, and we have no problem with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of a back-and-forth. רב ספרא is finishing his rejection of רבא's rule that a person should not pause in the middle of the פסוק 'ברוך הבא בשם ה''.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had worried that a pause would make the words sound like a separate, wrong statement. רב ספרא answers that the second half of the phrase obviously completes the first, so no one will misunderstand. A pause therefore does no harm.

keyTerms.meaning: 'משה!', a respectful (here half-teasing) title for a great scholar
Did you speak well?! A rhetorical way of saying 'That is not correct'
There and here, meaning in both cases
And we have no problem with it

steps.confusionAlert: Calling רבא 'משה' is not a mistake about his name. It is an honorific meaning 'you great teacher'. It is used here with a bit of sarcasm to introduce a rejection.

phrases.english: Moshe, did you speak well?!
phrases.notes: רב ספרא addressing רבא respectfully but critically

phrases.english: Rather, both there and here
phrases.notes: Covers both pausing and not pausing

phrases.english: it is just completing the matter,
and we have no problem with it.
phrases.notes: The closing parenthesis ends a bracketed section in the printed text

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ספרא's rejection of רבא's statement about 'ברוך הבא', which began on the previous amud.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's rule against pausing in 'ברוך הבא בשם ה''.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The feared misunderstanding will not happen, because the second half obviously completes the phrase.

steps.title: רבא: say 'יהא שמיה רבא מברך' together
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that in קדיש one should not pause between 'יהא שמיה רבא' and 'מברך'. The words should be said together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A person should not say 'May His great name' and then, after a pause, 'be blessed'. Rather, he should say 'May His great name be blessed' together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, similar rule about not pausing. This time the phrase is from קדיש: 'יהא שמיה רבא מברך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you stop after 'יהא שמיה רבא', it could sound like a complete sentence with a different meaning ('May His name be great'), cut off from 'מברך'. רבא therefore wants the whole phrase said in one breath. This has the same structure as his rule about 'ברוך הבא'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'May His great name', the opening of the main response in קַדִּישׁ

phrases.english: Rava said:
A person should not say
'May His great name' and then [separately] 'be blessed',
rather, 'May His great name be blessed' together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling by רבא about pausing, applied to קדיש instead of the פסוק 'ברוך הבא'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Say 'יהא שמיה רבא מברך' without a pause in the middle.

steps.title: רב ספרא rejects רבא again for the same reason
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא rejects רבא's קדיש rule with the same argument: 'מברך' clearly completes the phrase, so pausing is harmless.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to him: 'משה, did you speak well?! Rather, both there and here, it is just completing the matter, and we have no problem with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא answers רבא's second rule with exactly the same words he used for the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא really does repeat the whole rejection, because now it applies to a new case, קדיש. The logic is identical: listeners understand that 'מברך' belongs to the phrase. So a pause does not change the meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disputes רבא here

steps.whatToRemember: In both cases (ברוך הבא and יהא שמיה רבא), רב ספרא holds that pausing is fine. The completing words make the meaning clear.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to him:
Moshe, did you speak well?!
Rather, both there and here
it is just completing the matter,
and we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא: מֹשֶׁה, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects רבא's rule from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the requirement to say 'יהא שמיה רבא מברך' without pausing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'מברך' obviously completes the phrase, so the pause causes no misunderstanding.

steps.title: Repeating and adding verses in הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'where they repeat' and brings a ברייתא: רבי repeated certain verses in הלל, and רבי אלעזר בן פרטא added more.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה says:] 'In a place where they are accustomed to repeat.' It was taught: רבי repeats things in it [הלל]. רבי אלעזר בן פרטא adds things in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה, about repeating verses in הלל. It brings a ברייתא describing what two תנאים did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that repeating verses is an old practice. רבי repeated certain verses. רבי אלעזר בן פרטא went further and 'added' things, which is unclear and sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where the custom is

phrases.english: 'In a place where they are accustomed to repeat.'
It was taught: Rabbi repeats things in it.
phrases.notes: 'רבי' means רבי יהודה הנשיא; 'it' means הלל

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פַּרְטָא מוֹסִיף בָּהּ דְּבָרִים.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Perata adds things in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא returns to explain the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי repeated verses in הלל, and רבי אלעזר בן פרטא added further repetitions.

steps.title: What did רבי אלעזר בן פרטא add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'adding' means in the practice of רבי אלעזר בן פרטא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question to set up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one would add new words to הלל, so 'מוסיף' needs an explanation. The question is not a challenge. It only asks for the meaning of the word.

phrases.english: What does he add?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of 'מוסיף' from the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly רבי אלעזר בן פרטא added to הלל.

steps.title: אביי: he repeated from 'אודך' onward
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רבי אלעזר בן פרטא added repetitions to the verses from 'אודך' until the end of the chapter.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He adds to repeat from 'I will thank You' and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. The 'adding' means repeating more verses, starting at 'אודך כי עניתני'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the text of הלל. 'Adding' simply means extending the repetition to more verses. This matches the custom many still keep today of saying each verse from 'אודך' twice.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I will thank You', the verse in תהלים קיח where the repetition begins

steps.whatToRemember: The repeating of verses from 'אודך' in הלל goes back to רבי אלעזר בן פרטא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the familiar practice of saying 'אודך' through the end of הלל twice.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
He adds to repeat
from 'I will thank You' and onward.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Adding' means extending the repetition to the verses from 'אודך' to the end.

steps.title: אביי: the ברכה before הלל is required
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's words 'where they bless, he blesses', אביי says custom decides only the ברכה after הלל. The ברכה before הלל is a real מצוה everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה says:] 'To bless, he should bless.' אביי said: They taught this only regarding afterwards, but beforehand, it is a מצוה to bless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה. אביי limits it: depending on custom applies only to the ברכה after הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made the ברכה sound fully dependent on local custom. אביי narrows this. The ברכה before הלל is a required מצוה wherever you are, and only the ending ברכה depends on custom.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only about (limits a ruling)
It is a מצוה to make a ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the משנה as saying the whole ברכה on הלל is optional custom. אביי says only the ending ברכה depends on custom. The opening ברכה is required.

phrases.english: '[Where accustomed] to bless, he should bless.'
Abaye said:
They taught this only regarding afterwards,
but beforehand, it is a מצוה to bless.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבָרֵךְ — יְבָרֵךְ. אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְאַחֲרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new phrase of the משנה is explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Custom decides only the ברכה after הלל. The ברכה before הלל is always required.

steps.title: שמואל: every מצוה gets a blessing before it is done
steps.stepSummary: אביי supports his ruling with שמואל's general rule: for every מצוה, the ברכה is said 'עובר לעשייתן', before doing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: For all the מצוות, one blesses over them 'over' [before] their performance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for אביי's ruling. It is a general rule from שמואל that a ברכה comes before doing any מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every מצוה needs a ברכה before it, הלל is no exception. So the opening ברכה is required by this general rule, not by local custom.

keyTerms.meaning: All the מצוות, every one of them
'Over' their performance, meaning before doing them
He makes a ברכה on them

steps.whyThisMatters: 'עובר לעשייתן' is a basic rule of ברכות that appears all over the תלמוד and in halacha. We make the ברכה before doing a מצוה.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
For all the מצוות,
one blesses over them before their performance.
phrases.notes: 'עובר' literally means 'passing', and here it means 'ahead of'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for אביי's statement.
steps.raayaObject: The ברכה before הלל is a real מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's rule that every מצוה is blessed 'עובר לעשייתן'.

steps.title: How do we know 'over' means 'before'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof that the word 'עובר' means going ahead or before.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where is it implied that this word 'over' is language meaning 'before'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the wording of שמואל's rule. This sets up a series of proofs from פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עובר' normally means 'passing', which could seem unclear. The גמרא wants a source showing it means 'ahead of'.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where is it implied?
Language of going first or preceding

phrases.english: And from where is it implied that this word 'over'
is language of preceding?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the meaning of a word in step 8.

steps.title: Proof from אחימעץ overtaking the כושי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a פסוק where אחימעץ ran and 'ויעבור' (passed ahead of) the כושי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן בר יצחק said, for it is written: 'And אחימעץ ran by the way of the plain and overtook the כושי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: a פסוק uses 'ויעבור' for running ahead of someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחימעץ was racing the כושי and got ahead of him. 'ויעבור' there clearly means 'went before', so 'עובר' can mean 'ahead of'.

keyTerms.meaning: A messenger in שמואל ב יח

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק דִּכְתִיב:
phrases.english: As Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said, for it is written:
'And Achimaatz ran by the way of the plain
and overtook the Cushite.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק דִּכְתִיב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ויעבור את הכושי' means he got ahead of the Cushite.

steps.title: אביי's proof from יעקב passing before his family
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a different פסוק: 'והוא עבר לפניהם', יעקב went ahead of his family.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: From here: 'And he passed before them.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers another source for the same point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב walked out in front of his family to meet עשו. Here the word 'עבר' appears together with 'לפניהם', which makes the meaning 'ahead of' even clearer.

phrases.english: Abaye said: From here:
'And he passed before them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative proof for the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'והוא עבר לפניהם' shows that 'עבר' means going ahead.

steps.title: A third proof from the king passing before them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a third פסוק: 'ויעבור מלכם לפניהם וה' בראשם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say from here: 'And their king passed before them, and ה׳ at their head.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more possible source, this time from מיכה, for the same meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פסוק the king leading the people is 'ויעבור לפניהם', parallel to 'בראשם' (at their head). The parallel confirms that 'עבר' means leading in front. All three proofs reach the same conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another option)

steps.whatToRemember: 'עובר לעשייתן' means the ברכה comes before the מצוה. Three פסוקים show that 'עבר' can mean 'go ahead of'.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say from here:
'And their king passed before them
and ה׳ at their head.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third alternative proof for the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ויעבור מלכם לפניהם' paired with 'בראשם' shows that 'עבר' means leading in front.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'עובר' means 'before', so every ברכה on a מצוה is said before doing it.

steps.title: New משנה: buying a לולב during שביעית
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that someone who buys a לולב during שביעית receives the אתרוג as a gift, because one may not buy an אתרוג during שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who buys a לולב from his fellow during שביעית, [the seller] gives him an אתרוג as a gift, because he is not permitted to buy it during שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with the problem of buying the ארבעה מינים during שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אתרוג is a fruit and has קדושת שביעית, so money paid for it takes on that holiness. The seller here is assumed to be an עם הארץ, who may not be handed such money (steps 17-18). A לולב does not carry this holiness and can be paid for, so the buyer pays for the לולב and receives the אתרוג as a free gift.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say an אתרוג from שביעית is not a valid אתרוג. The fruit is fine for the מצוה. The issue is only about paying for it, because the payment money would become holy and end up with an עם הארץ, so the אתרוג is given as a gift.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the topic of fruits with קדושת שביעית and how the ארבעה מינים are obtained in a שמיטה year, which the גמרא will analyze next.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who buys a lulav from his fellow during the Sabbatical Year —
[the seller] gives him an etrog as a gift,
because he is not permitted to buy it during the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During שביעית, buy the לולב and receive the אתרוג as a gift, since an אתרוג may not be sold commercially.

steps.title: What if the seller refuses to give the אתרוג as a gift?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what happens if the seller will not give the אתרוג for free, as the משנה assumed.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: If the seller did not want to give him the אתרוג as a gift, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the new משנה. It asks about a case the משנה did not cover: what if the seller won't give the אתרוג as a gift?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's solution only works if the seller agrees to give the אתרוג for free. If he insists on being paid, the buyer seems stuck, because paying directly for an אתרוג in שביעית is a problem. The גמרא wants a practical way out.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that comes after the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the Talmudic discussion on the משנה.

phrases.english: If he (the seller) did not want to give it to him as a gift,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא רָצָה לִיתֵּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה, מַהוּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a case the משנה (step 13) did not address. Step 15 answers it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the buyer gets an אתרוג in שביעית if the seller refuses to give it free.

steps.title: רב הונא: hide the אתרוג's price inside the לולב's price
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the buyer pays a higher price for the לולב, which quietly covers the cost of the אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: He folds the price of the אתרוג into the price of the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a practical answer. The buyer pays more for the לולב, so the seller is paid for the אתרוג without the money being called payment for the אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No money is officially given for the אתרוג, so the שביעית problem is avoided. The seller still ends up fully paid. The key word is מַבְלִיעַ, meaning to 'swallow up' one price inside another.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer here
Folds in, hides one price inside another (literally 'swallows')

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
He incorporates for him the price of the etrog into the lulav.
phrases.notes: He pays an inflated price for the לולב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַבְלַיע לֵיהּ דְּמֵי אֶתְרוֹג בְּלוּלָב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Pay an inflated price for the לולב that covers the אתרוג.

steps.title: Why not just pay for the אתרוג openly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: why the trick? Let the buyer simply pay for the אתרוג directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him just give him the money for it openly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב הונא's trick. If the seller ends up paid anyway, why not pay for the אתרוג openly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes there is nothing wrong with paying for the אתרוג. If so, hiding the price looks pointless. This forces the גמרא to explain what is actually wrong with paying directly.

phrases.english: And let him give it to him directly?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why רב הונא's method in step 15 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's method of hiding the price
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the seller is paid anyway, the indirect method seems unnecessary. Direct payment should be just as good.

steps.title: שביעית money may not be handed to an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: The answer: money paid for שביעית produce becomes holy, and it may not be given to an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because one may not hand over money paid for שביעית produce to an עם הארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why direct payment is a problem. Money paid for שביעית fruit takes on שביעית holiness, and we may not hand it to an עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ is not trusted to follow the rules for holy שביעית money, so he might misuse it. Paying openly for the אתרוג would give him such money. Hiding the payment inside the לולב's price means the money is not officially for שביעית fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce of the Sabbatical year, which has special holiness
An unlearned person not trusted to keep these laws carefully

steps.confusionAlert: The money itself becomes holy. Holiness from שביעית fruit passes onto the money paid for it, so the problem is handing over holy money, not the act of buying.

phrases.english: Because one may not transfer
money paid for Sabbatical-Year produce to an am ha'aretz.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מוֹסְרִין דְּמֵי פֵּירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית לְעַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reveals a hidden halachic problem that justifies the method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Paying directly is harmless, so the trick is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Direct payment puts holy שביעית money in an עם הארץ's hands, so the price must be hidden.

steps.title: ברייתא source: limits on giving שביעית money, and how to fix it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא backs up the rule. One may not give an עם הארץ more שביעית money than the cost of three meals. If he did, he moves the holiness onto produce in his own house.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: One may not give an עם הארץ money from שביעית produce worth more than three meals. If he did give it, he should say: 'This money is redeemed onto produce that I have in my house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as the source for the rule just stated. The ברייתא also gives a fix for someone who already handed over too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to three meals' worth is allowed, since the עם הארץ will most likely just spend it on food, which is a proper use. Above that is not allowed. If he gave more, he transfers the holiness off the money and onto his own produce at home, so the money in the עם הארץ's hands is now ordinary.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a source)
Redeemed, made ordinary by moving the holiness elsewhere

steps.whatToRemember: An אתרוג in שביעית is bought by hiding its price in the לולב. The reason: holy שביעית money may not go to an עם הארץ beyond three meals' worth. If it already did, the buyer redeems the money onto his own produce.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the holiness of שביעית fruit passes onto the money paid for it. It also shows that this holiness can be moved off the money and onto other produce.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
One may not transfer money of Sabbatical-Year produce
to an am ha'aretz
more than the value of food for three meals.
And if he did transfer it, he should say:
Behold, this money shall be deconsecrated

phrases.aramaic: עַל פֵּירוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתִי,
phrases.english: onto produce that I have in my house,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא does not end here. It continues on the next amud, which tells what he then does with the produce in his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין מוֹסְרִין דְּמֵי פֵּירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית לְעַם הָאָרֶץ
